graphEvents.label: Stealth and site terms of service

label: Signed-in profiles: Bladebro `rb` can act in authenticated sessions and "Actions in a signed-in profile can affect your account"; the operator must choose the profile/account before handoff, `attach` keeps a caller-owned browser open, `clone` auto-refreshes logins/cookies, and `profile` needs the browser closed (Chrome 136+ refuses remote debugging on the default data dir). Mitigation R-SEC-1: owned-profile default with BLADE_HOME/BLADE_FRESH isolation, explicit real-browser request, operator profile/account selection, `attach` for caller-owned browsers, `rb pause`/`resume` gating, no `--account` on `aside mcp`/`aside repl`, single-writer lock per account/profile, and per-session capture redaction.

Stealth and site terms of service: STEALTH_BENCH.md records 68/80 (85.0%) anti-bot sites passed with no proxy/CAPTCHA solver/fingerprint farm and a `blocked:` verdict limit in the README; this is an anti-detection capability whose ToS/legal use is an operator gate. Mitigation R-SEC-2: operator ToS gate before real-browser use on a target site, never evade CAPTCHAs/anti-bot walls/access controls where that breaches terms or law, treat `blocked:` as terminal, log pinned v4.8.2 usage, prefer the agent-browser lane where stealth is not required.

npm binary supply chain: `npm install -g bladebro` pulls optional native packages (`bladebro-darwin-arm64`/`bladebro-darwin-x64`), has no postinstall script, and publishes standalone binaries with `.sha256` sidecars; v4.8.2 digests are `sha256:7324e502...` (arm64) and `sha256:d839f5f8...` (x64), and upstream ships fast. Mitigation R-SEC-3: install stays a 006 operator stop-for-yes, pin v4.8.2 plus read date, verify resolved native package SHA-256 against release sidecars with `shasum -a 256 -c`, prefer the standalone binary for higher assurance, re-verify flags against the installed binary, and staged rollback with `npm uninstall -g bladebro` then data-root removal only after confirming no needed named sessions.

004 REQ-002 mapping is complete and disjoint: R-SEC-1 -> signed-in profiles (Finding 1), R-SEC-2 -> stealth & site terms of service (Finding 2), R-SEC-3 -> npm binary supply chain (Finding 3); each KQ7 risk family in research.md now maps to one quotable 004 safety rule, closing the KQ7 answered-means bar.
